newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's state oil firm denies gas deal with Total.
newsitem.headline: Iran's state oil firm denies gas deal with Total.

text.p: The National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) on Sunday denied that Iran had signed a $3.5 billion deal with France's Total to develop the South Pars gas field.

Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told a news conference on Sunday that Total had signed an agreement worth $3.5 billion with the Islamic republic's oil minister for the further development of South Pars.
"The foreign minister's statement is not correct as such. NIOC and the Ministry of Petroleum have not finalised any agreement with either Total or Shell," said an NIOC official.
"Our negotiations with the two sides are still continuing," the official added.
Velayati did not say when the deal was signed to further develop the field, which is expected to become the backbone of Iran's plans to export gas to Turkey, Pakistan, India and eventually Europe.
Consortia led by Total and Royal Dutch/Shell have been in the race for the South Pars contract.
